page: Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is an x86_64 virtual machine belonging to the Laosv4 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. It includes 2880 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth present notable tradeoffs. While write memory bandwidth for large blocks and multi-core CPU benchmarks sit in the average tier, read-only memory bandwidth is weak, falling into the bottom 25%. Similarly, database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput are weak, indicating potential bottlenecks for high-throughput transactional workloads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the L4aos_v4 offers a high local storage capacity of 2880 GB relative to its 4 vCPU compute footprint, making it a dense option for storage-heavy workloads without requiring larger compute tiers. The instance is well-suited for workloads that benefit from strong single-core execution and high local storage capacity, such as localized data processing, text processing, and moderate file-serving tasks, though it is less optimal for memory-read-intensive databases.
